topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I must say, the way I handled it was nothing short of remarkable. When I saw them, all grown up with the same laughter that once filled our treehouse, I simply stepped into the story as if nothing had changed. I told tales of our past, weaving memories with such finesse that even I couldn’t tell which were real and which were spun on the loom of the moment. Their eyes lit up, a recognition forming, and I knew I had painted a picture where I belonged. We laughed, and the past didn’t matter, only this new beginning, where I was still the indispensable piece of their puzzle.
